**Test image features:**
- Longitudinal cross-section of a tomato stem
- Very dark brown/black internal pith and vascular tissue
- Dramatic contrast: dark inner core vs. intact green outer cortex
- Dark discoloration runs continuously along the stem length

**Key reference comparison:**
- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato** (Bugwood_18) was the only reference that directly showed a longitudinal stem cut, revealing brownish internal vascular/pith discoloration — the same diagnostic technique used in the test image
- **Bacterial_Wilt** references showed stem pieces in water with ooze (different diagnostic presentation)
- **Verticillium_Wilt** references all showed leaf/whole plant symptoms, none showing the stem cross-section pattern
- All other classes showed either leaf symptoms, field-wilted plants, or microscopic spores — none matching a stem cross-section

The extensive dark, almost black pith discoloration visible in this longitudinal cut is a hallmark diagnostic of Bacterial Canker (*Clavibacter michiganensis*), which causes aggressive internal vascular and pith browning in tomato stems. The reference class Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato directly depicted this same type of stem dissection.
